constructs.label: `now()`
constructs.note: Carbon; the compiled side follows the **request clock** (M33) - the wall clock diverged.

constructs.label: `today()`
constructs.note: Carbon at midnight (UTC); the request clock again.

constructs.label: `abort_if()`
constructs.note: Answers null unless it aborts; the status + the message are Laravel's.

constructs.label: `abort_unless()`
constructs.note: The mirror of abort_if.

constructs.label: `Log::info()`
constructs.note: The platform log (the Workers console) is the padanan for the app log file.

constructs.label: `new RuntimeException()`
constructs.note: The **built-in** exceptions only; the class name + the message are kept, so the 500 matches.

constructs.label: `throw_if()`
constructs.note: Throws the given error when the condition says so.

constructs.label: `redirect()->with()`
constructs.note: Flashes into the session for the next request; the proof is the session payload + the Location.

constructs.label: `redirect()->withInput()`
constructs.note: Flashes `_old_input` (everything except the `dontFlash` fields).

constructs.label: `redirect()->withErrors()`
constructs.note: Flashes the error bag in the `ViewErrorBag` shape (the M19 validation flow writes the same shape).

constructs.label: `redirect()->away()`
constructs.note: An absolute external URL (the compiled redirect keeps it absolute).

constructs.label: `back()`
constructs.note: The Referer, or the session's `url.previous`, or `/`.

constructs.label: `Str::slug()`
constructs.note: The PHP-exact subset (slug/limit/upper/lower/studly/camel/snake/kebab/title/contains/startsWith/endsWith/after/before/length/replace*/squish/ucfirst/ucwords/ascii) - every value is verified against the real Laravel.

constructs.label: `env()`
constructs.note: The build-time config dump is the padanan (the edge has no .env); only the app.* keys are mapped.

constructs.label: `data_get()`
constructs.note: Dot/array access on an array or an object (the `*` wildcard is not ported).

constructs.label: `tap()`
constructs.note: Passes the value through a closure (the closure support exists).

constructs.label: `report()`
constructs.note: Reports an exception to the platform log (it does not answer it).

constructs.label: `cache()` (the helper)
constructs.note: The helper form of the `Cache` facade (the facade compiles).

constructs.label: `session([...])` (the array form)
constructs.note: The array form writes many keys: `session()->put([...])`.

constructs.label: `Event::dispatch()` (an event object)
constructs.note: The listener is a class, so the build compiles it (the event classes + the listeners, dist/src/classes.generated.mjs). The dispatch is synchronous, like Laravel's.

constructs.label: `Event::dispatch()` (an event name)
constructs.note: An event *name* has no class: the edge cannot know which listener answers, so the dispatch would be a silent no-op - dispatch the event object instead.

constructs.label: `Gate::allows()`
constructs.note: The policy is compiled at build time: the abilities, the guest rules, the before() hook.

constructs.label: `Gate::allows()` (the class-level check)
constructs.note: Laravel shifts the class name away before the ability is called.

constructs.label: `Gate::authorize()`
constructs.note: It throws an AuthorizationException (a 403) - the edge has no such error view yet.

constructs.label: `Gate::any()`
constructs.note: Only `allows()` and `denies()` compile.

constructs.label: `Gate::define()`
constructs.note: A closure is not compiled - the global Gate registrations stay a port.

constructs.label: `Gate::before()`
constructs.note: The global Gate callbacks are not compiled (the policies are).

constructs.label: `Mail::to()->send()`
constructs.note: A mailable renders its own Blade view: the compiled rung would have to compile the mailable, render that view and produce the very same payload - and the shadow harness would have to compare the mail payload byte for byte (it cannot today: the log format differs). **Not mapped yet** (a milestone of its own).

constructs.label: `Queue::push()`
constructs.note: The queue is asynchronous and the edge has no consumer: the job would never run (a silent no-op), so the byte parity with Laravel is impossible. The job class compiles (M39c) - the blocker is the consumer, not the class.

constructs.label: `Storage::disk()` (the default disk)
constructs.note: The default disk is the compiled object store (the D1 blob store, or R2 when bound).

constructs.label: `Storage::disk()` (a named disk)
constructs.note: A named disk needs a bucket of its own (R2 asks for a credit card); the compiled rung has one store.

constructs.label: `Cache::tags()`
constructs.note: Tags need a KV/Redis-shaped store; the D1 `database` store has no tags (Laravel throws there too).

constructs.label: Blade `@extends` (a layout)
constructs.note: The sections travel to the layout (the shadow harness proves the bytes).

constructs.label: `Model::paginate()`
constructs.note: The LengthAwarePaginator (the items, the total, the pages, the URLs) + the pagination links (the framework's `pagination::tailwind` view is compiled at build time).

constructs.label: The translation helper (`__()`)
constructs.note: The strings are dumped at build time (the app's lang/ files + the framework's fallback); the place-holders are replaced like Laravel does.

constructs.label: A PHP cast (`(string) $x`)
constructs.note: The scalar casts with PHP's own semantics: (string), (int), (bool), (float).

constructs.label: Route-model binding (a typed param)
constructs.note: The model comes from the route segment (Laravel's implicit binding); a missing model is a 404.

constructs.label: Eloquent relations (`$post->comments()`)
constructs.note: A relation is not compiled: the build stops (LW003). The compiled way to read a relation is the eager-loaded subset (`with()`).

constructs.label: File upload (`$request->file()`)
constructs.note: The multipart body is parsed at the edge: the file object carries the metadata (the name, the type the browser declared, the size) and the store (the app's default disk). Byte-proven by the shadow harness.

constructs.label: The upload is stored (`$file->storeAs()`)
constructs.note: The object store (the D1 blob store on the free plan, R2 with a bucket of its own): the path is the disk-relative one Laravel returns (trim($path.'/'.$name, '/')).

constructs.label: The upload is stored under a random name (`$file->store()`)
constructs.note: The name is a random hash (Str::random(40)) + the extension; the extension comes from the type the browser declared (Laravel sniffs the content with finfo).

constructs.label: The content type of the upload (`$file->getMimeType()`)
constructs.note: The content type is read from the file's bytes (finfo): the edge cannot sniff the content like PHP does, so the build stops (LW003).

constructs.label: A `mimes` rule on an upload
constructs.note: The `mimes` rule compares the extension the content sniffs (finfo): the edge has only the type the browser declared, so the build stops (LW002) instead of answering differently.

constructs.label: The files bag as a method (`$request->files()`)
constructs.note: In Laravel `$request->files` is a property (Symfony's FileBag), not a method: the build stops (LW002) and points at `$request->file()` / `$request->allFiles()`.

constructs.label: An `OPTIONS` route
constructs.note: The compiled side answers Laravel's automatic OPTIONS response (200 + the Allow header - byte-proven); a CORS config makes the build skip the route.

constructs.label: A relation read as a property (`$post->comments`)
constructs.note: A relation (or an accessor) read as a property is not compiled: the build stops (LW003). It used to answer null - a wrong answer, silently.

constructs.label: A rule object (`Rule::file()->max()`)
constructs.note: A rule object is a class: the compiled validator evaluates the string rules only, so the rule would be silently ignored and the validation would differ. The build stops and names what it would take: the kernel validator must evaluate the rule object, the FormRequest must be compiled and its prepared input merged into the validated data.

constructs.label: A rule object in a FormRequest
constructs.note: The FormRequest dump reads the rules Laravel itself builds: a rule object is found there and the build stops ("the rules use a rule object (Illuminate\Validation\Rules\File) - the compiled rung evaluates the string rules only"). The dump's reason reaches the operator - it is not swallowed by a generic message anymore.

constructs.label: `prepareForValidation()` (overridden)
constructs.note: The FormRequest dump sees the overridden hook: "prepareForValidation() is overridden - the compiled rung does not run it (the validated input would differ)". The build stops and the reason reaches the operator.

constructs.label: A listener that injects a service
constructs.class_php:
<?php
namespace App\Listeners;

use App\Events\PostPublished;
use App\Services\Mailer;

class L
{
    public function __construct(private Mailer $mailer)
    {
    }

    public function handle(PostPublished $event): void
    {
        $this->mailer->send($event);
    }
}
constructs.note: The edge instantiates the listener itself: it cannot inject a service, so the constructor dependency is a build error. It used to compile - the property stayed undefined and the request died at runtime (a 500 the build said nothing about).

constructs.label: A queued listener (`ShouldQueue`)
constructs.class_php:
<?php
namespace App\Listeners;

use App\Events\PostPublished;

class L
{
    public function handle(PostPublished $event): void
    {
        $event->id;
    }
}
constructs.note: Laravel pushes a queued listener to the queue (it runs later); the edge has no queue consumer, so running it inline would be a different behaviour. The build stops and the route that dispatches the event names the reason.
